sys_update_xml.name: sys_transform_entry_0acc28562b041b54eb1cfbfdf291bfd7
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_transform_entry"><sys_transform_entry action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><choice_action>create</choice_action><coalesce>false</coalesce><coalesce_case_sensitive>false</coalesce_case_sensitive><coalesce_empty_fields>false</coalesce_empty_fields><date_format>yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss</date_format><map display_value="HP WXP Alert to Incident">ccf5939f2b750710eb1cfbfdf291bf79</map><reference_value_field/><source_field>[Script]</source_field><source_script><![CDATA[answer = (function transformEntry(source) {

    // Set with state and close_code. Otherwise keep what the incident has (Copy empty fields is on).
    var status = alertStatus(source.u_status);
    if (status === 'FIXED')
        return 'Resolved automatically: HP WXP reported this alert as fixed.';
    if (status === 'DISMISSED')
        return 'Cancelled automatically: HP WXP reported this alert as dismissed.';
    return target.getValue('close_notes');

    /** u_status arrives as a stringified {"name":"NEW","value":"New"}; a bare "NEW" also works. */
    function alertStatus(field) {
        var raw = ('' + (field || '')).trim();
        if (!raw)
            return '';
        try {
            var parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
            return ('' + (parsed.name || parsed.value || '')).toUpperCase();
        } catch (e) {
            return raw.toUpperCase();
        }
    }

})(source);]]></source_script><source_table>x_hpws_wrkfrcexpam_hp_alert_inc_import_set</source_table><sys_class_name>sys_transform_entry</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>saurav.sarkar</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-10-22 12:25:25</sys_created_on><sys_id>0acc28562b041b54eb1cfbfdf291bfd7</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>[Script]</sys_name><sys_package display_value="HP WXP Alert Management" source="x_hpws_wrkfrcexpam">fb68f3922bf94750eb1cfbfdf291bf2b</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="HP WXP Alert Management">fb68f3922bf94750eb1cfbfdf291bf2b</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_transform_entry_0acc28562b041b54eb1cfbfdf291bfd7</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>saurav.sarkar</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-10-22 12:25:25</sys_updated_on><target_field>close_notes</target_field><target_table>incident</target_table><use_source_script>true</use_source_script></sys_transform_entry></record_update>

HP WXP Alert Management – Application Privacy Policy

HP WXP Alert Management (the "Application") is a ServiceNow application provided by HP Inc. ("HP"). It connects HP Workforce Experience Platform (HP WXP) to your ServiceNow instance: it receives device alerts from HP WXP, creates and updates ServiceNow incidents from them, and reports incident status back to HP WXP. This policy describes how the Application handles data. It supplements the HP Privacy Statement, which governs HP's processing of personal data.

1. What Data is Collected

The Application receives the following data from HP WXP:

  • Alert details: alert ID, display ID, title, description, type, subtype, status, category, subcategory, impact, urgency, alert rule ID, source location and timestamps
  • Device details: device name, serial number and model
  • Company details: company name and HP WXP tenant ID
  • Details of the affected user, where provided by HP WXP: user ID, user name and email address
  • The complete alert message as received, which is kept in the Incoming Alert Log

The Application also stores the following configuration in your ServiceNow instance:

  • HP WXP tenant and connection settings, including the API key
  • The group to notify if the integration fails

2. How the Data is Used

The collected data is used to:

  • Create and update ServiceNow incidents from HP WXP alerts, including the short description, description, category, impact, urgency, assignment group and a work note with the device and company details
  • Set the incident caller by matching the affected user's email address or user name to an existing active ServiceNow user
  • Link the incident to the matching configuration item using the device serial number
  • Keep the incident in step with the alert, for example by resolving the incident when the alert is fixed or dismissed
  • Report incident status back to HP WXP
  • Email the configured group if the integration fails
  • Support troubleshooting and auditing through the Incoming Alert Log and system logs

3. Data Sharing with Third Parties

The Application communicates only with HP WXP. It sends:

  • Incident status updates: alert and incident identifiers, incident number, state, priority and resolution date, and an identifier for the assigned user (no names or email addresses)
  • Requests for the list of customer tenants, for HP partners who manage several customers

HP WXP can also read the incident categories, subcategories and assignment groups configured in your instance, so that alert rules can be set up.

No other ServiceNow data is shared. HP may use service providers to operate HP WXP, under the terms of the HP Privacy Statement and your agreement with HP. The Application does not sell data.

4. Data Transfer, Storage, and Security

  • All data transfers are encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher.
  • Data received by the Application is stored in your ServiceNow instance and is subject to your instance's data residency, backup and retention settings.
  • Requests from HP WXP to the Application must be authenticated.
  • Access to the Application's data and configuration is restricted through role-based access controls.
  • The HP WXP API key is stored encrypted and is used only to connect to HP WXP.
  • Staging records created during alert import are deleted automatically after 30 days. Incidents and Incoming Alert Log records are kept according to your organisation's retention policies.

5. Use of Artificial Intelligence

The Application does not use artificial intelligence (AI) or Large Language Model (LLM) services and does not send data to any AI provider. For information about HP's approach to AI, see HP's AI Governance Principles.

6. Roles and Responsibilities

Your organisation controls the incident and user data held in your ServiceNow instance, including who can access it and how long it is kept. HP processes data received from the Application as part of the HP WXP service, in line with the HP Privacy Statement and your agreement with HP.

7. Privacy Requests and Contact

  • HP Privacy Central
  • To make a privacy request or give privacy feedback, use the HP privacy request form.
  • For questions about the Application, contact HP Global Support at workforceexperience@hp.com.

Last updated: October 2026

sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_script_include"><sys_script_include action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><access>package_private</access><active>true</active><api_name>x_hpws_wrkfrcexpam.AlertConfigLookups</api_name><caller_access/><client_callable>false</client_callable><description>Builds the assignment group / category / subcategory lists the WXP alert-configuration page needs to populate its three dependent dropdowns, plus the ETag that lets the caller skip the payload when nothing has changed. Backs the GET /lookups resource of the snow_alert_config Scripted REST API.</description><mobile_callable>false</mobile_callable><name>AlertConfigLookups</name><sandbox_callable>false</sandbox_callable><script><![CDATA[var AlertConfigLookups = Class.create();
AlertConfigLookups.prototype = {

    GROUP_QUERY:       'active=true',
    CATEGORY_QUERY:    'name=incident^element=category^inactive=false^language=en',
    SUBCATEGORY_QUERY: 'name=incident^element=subcategory^inactive=false^language=en',

    /**
     * Both choice lists in one query, for the ETag. '^OR' binds only to the condition
     * immediately before it, so 'element=category^...^ORelement=subcategory' silently
     * matched nothing on the subcategory side and subcategory edits never invalidated
     * the cache. 'elementIN' covers both.
     */
    CHOICE_QUERY:      'name=incident^inactive=false^language=en^elementINcategory,subcategory',

    initialize: function () {},

    /**
     * Everything the alert-configuration page needs, in one response. No cap - the caller
     * receives the full lists and filters client-side.
     */
    getLookups: function () {
        return {
            assignmentGroups: this._assignmentGroups(),
            categories: this._choices(this.CATEGORY_QUERY),
            subcategoriesByCategory: this._subcategoriesByCategory()
        };
    },

    /**
     * Weak validator over everything that can change the payload: edits to groups, groups
     * appearing or disappearing, edits to the choice lists, and choices appearing or
     * disappearing. Timestamps are compressed because a quoted header value is easier to
     * handle without spaces and colons in it.
     */
    getETag: function () {
        var parts = [
            'lookups',
            this._compress(this._maxUpdated('sys_user_group', this.GROUP_QUERY)),
            this._count('sys_user_group', this.GROUP_QUERY),
            this._compress(this._maxUpdated('sys_choice', this.CHOICE_QUERY)),
            this._count('sys_choice', this.CHOICE_QUERY)
        ];
        return 'W/"' + parts.join('-') + '"';
    },

    _assignmentGroups: function () {
        var groups = [];
        var group = new GlideRecordSecure('sys_user_group');
        group.addEncodedQuery(this.GROUP_QUERY);
        group.orderBy('name');
        group.query();
        while (group.next()) {
            groups.push({
                id: group.getUniqueValue(),
                name: group.getValue('name')
            });
        }
        return groups;
    },

    _choices: function (encodedQuery) {
        var choices = [];
        var choice = new GlideRecordSecure('sys_choice');
        choice.addEncodedQuery(encodedQuery);
        choice.orderBy('label');
        choice.query();
        while (choice.next()) {
            choices.push({
                value: choice.getValue('value'),
                label: choice.getValue('label')
            });
        }
        return choices;
    },

    /** Subcategories keyed by the category they hang off, so the caller can chain the dropdowns. */
    _subcategoriesByCategory: function () {
        var byCategory = {};
        var choice = new GlideRecordSecure('sys_choice');
        choice.addEncodedQuery(this.SUBCATEGORY_QUERY);
        choice.orderBy('label');
        choice.query();
        while (choice.next()) {
            var parent = choice.getValue('dependent_value');
            if (!parent)
                continue;
            if (!byCategory[parent])
                byCategory[parent] = [];
            byCategory[parent].push({
                value: choice.getValue('value'),
                label: choice.getValue('label')
            });
        }
        return byCategory;
    },

    /**
     * GlideRecordSecure rather than GlideAggregate: GlideAggregate.MAX('sys_updated_on') returns
     * stale data on this field. Per WEXFER-525 and endpoint plan section 6.8.
     */
    _maxUpdated: function (table, encodedQuery) {
        var gr = new GlideRecordSecure(table);
        gr.addEncodedQuery(encodedQuery);
        gr.orderByDesc('sys_updated_on');
        gr.setLimit(1);
        gr.query();
        return gr.next() ? (gr.getValue('sys_updated_on') || '') : '';
    },

    _count: function (table, encodedQuery) {
        var agg = new GlideAggregate(table);
        agg.addEncodedQuery(encodedQuery);
        agg.addAggregate('COUNT');
        agg.query();
        return agg.next() ? ('' + agg.getAggregate('COUNT')) : '0';
    },

    _compress: function (value) {
        return ('' + value).replace(/[^0-9A-Za-z]/g, '');
    },

    type: 'AlertConfigLookups'
};]]></script><sys_class_name>sys_script_include</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>saurav.sarkar</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-08-18 15:55:41</sys_created_on><sys_id>8c9d2a592b760b10eb1cfbfdf291bffe</sys_id><sys_mod_count>2</sys_mod_count><sys_name>AlertConfigLookups</sys_name><sys_package display_value="HP WXP Alert Management" source="x_hpws_wrkfrcexpam">fb68f3922bf94750eb1cfbfdf291bf2b</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="HP WXP Alert Management">fb68f3922bf94750eb1cfbfdf291bf2b</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_script_include_8c9d2a592b760b10eb1cfbfdf291bffe</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>aditi.khanna</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-10-09 14:00:44</sys_updated_on></sys_script_include></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: sys_transform_entry_bdcc28562b041b54eb1cfbfdf291bfcf
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_transform_entry"><sys_transform_entry action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><choice_action>ignore</choice_action><coalesce>false</coalesce><coalesce_case_sensitive>false</coalesce_case_sensitive><coalesce_empty_fields>false</coalesce_empty_fields><date_format>yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss</date_format><map display_value="HP WXP Alert to Incident">ccf5939f2b750710eb1cfbfdf291bf79</map><reference_value_field/><source_field>[Script]</source_field><source_script><![CDATA[answer = (function transformEntry(source) {

    // Set with state and close_notes: the 'Make close info mandatory when resolved or closed'
    // data policy applies to imports. Otherwise keep what the incident has (Copy empty fields is on).
    if (alertStatus(source.u_status) === 'FIXED')
        return 'Solution provided';
    return target.getValue('close_code');

    /** u_status arrives as a stringified {"name":"NEW","value":"New"}; a bare "NEW" also works. */
    function alertStatus(field) {
        var raw = ('' + (field || '')).trim();
        if (!raw)
            return '';
        try {
            var parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
            return ('' + (parsed.name || parsed.value || '')).toUpperCase();
        } catch (e) {
            return raw.toUpperCase();
        }
    }

})(source);]]></source_script><source_table>x_hpws_wrkfrcexpam_hp_alert_inc_import_set</source_table><sys_class_name>sys_transform_entry</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>saurav.sarkar</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-10-22 12:25:25</sys_created_on><sys_id>bdcc28562b041b54eb1cfbfdf291bfcf</sys_id><sys_mod_count>4</sys_mod_count><sys_name>[Script]</sys_name><sys_package display_value="HP WXP Alert Management" source="x_hpws_wrkfrcexpam">fb68f3922bf94750eb1cfbfdf291bf2b</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="HP WXP Alert Management">fb68f3922bf94750eb1cfbfdf291bf2b</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_transform_entry_bdcc28562b041b54eb1cfbfdf291bfcf</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>saurav.sarkar</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-10-22 14:20:36</sys_updated_on><target_field>close_code</target_field><target_table>incident</target_table><use_source_script>true</use_source_script></sys_transform_entry></record_update>
